title: Rare-earth tuning of magnetic entropy and interaction scales in K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ ($Ln$ = Yb, Gd) for adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration
authors: Yonglin Wang, Chuandi Zhang, Jianglong Zhang, Zihang Gao, Ziqi Li, Feiran Shen, Lunhua He, Peijie Sun, Hao Deng, Junsen Xiang, Wentao Jin
abstract: Adiabatic demagnetization refrigeration (ADR) based on frustrated rare-earth magnets provides a promising route toward helium-free sub-Kelvin cooling, while balancing magnetic entropy and interaction scales is essential for optimizing the ADR functionalities. Here we investigate the low-temperature magnetic and ADR properties of the alkali rare-earth double phosphates K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ ($Ln$ = Yb, Gd), which crystallize in a monoclinic $P2_1/m$ structure containing distorted isosceles triangular lattices of rare-earth ions. Magnetization and specific heat measurements confirm the absence of long-range magnetic ordering down to 0.1 K in both compounds. Direct quasi-ADR measurements demonstrate strongly contrasting refrigeration behaviors: K$_3$Yb(PO$_4$)$_2$ reaches a minimum temperature of 29.8 mK from an initial state of 2 K and 6 T, whereas K$_3$Gd(PO$_4$)$_2$ exhibits extended hold times below 150 mK associated with its larger magnetic entropy reservoir. Crystal-electric-field calculations confirm a $J_{\mathrm{eff}} = 1/2$ ground-state doublet in K$_3$Yb(PO$_4$)$_2$, while thermodynamic analysis based on magnetic entropy and interaction scales accounts for the distinct ADR performance of the two compounds. These results identify K$_3$$Ln$(PO$_4$)$_2$ as a chemically robust platform for rare-earth-tunable solid-state ADR.
summary: This paper investigates rare-earth double phosphates, $	ext{K}_3	ext{Ln}(	ext{PO}_4)_2$, as solid-state materials for achieving ultra-low temperatures via Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigeration (ADR). By comparing $	ext{Yb}$ and $	ext{Gd}$ compounds, the authors demonstrate that tuning the rare-earth element allows for engineering complementary cooling functionalities—from deep cooling to high entropy storage—within a single, stable material platform.
main_problem: The study aims to optimize Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigeration (ADR) by understanding and balancing the magnetic entropy and interaction scales within specific crystalline materials.
main_result: The $	ext{K}_3	ext{Ln}(	ext{PO}_4)_2$ family is established as a chemically robust and rare-earth-tunable platform for solid-state ADR, with $	ext{K}_3	ext{Yb}(	ext{PO}_4)_2$ reaching ultra-low temperatures and $	ext{K}_3	ext{Gd}(	ext{PO}_4)_2$ offering a large entropy reservoir.
method: The research combines low-temperature magnetic measurements (magnetization, specific heat) with direct quasi-ADR measurements and theoretical calculations (Crystal Electric Field theory) to analyze thermodynamic performance.
model_or_system: The physical system is the alkali rare-earth double phosphate $	ext{K}_3	ext{Ln}(	ext{PO}_4)_2$ ($	ext{Ln} = 	ext{Yb}, 	ext{Gd}$), which crystallizes in a monoclinic structure featuring rare-earth ions in distorted triangular lattices.
key_observables: Minimum attainable temperature (e.g., $29.8 	ext{ mK}$), extended hold times, magnetic entropy, specific heat, and magnetic susceptibility ($\chi(T)$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures ($\sim 0.1 	ext{ K}$ to $2 	ext{ K}$), magnetic fields up to $7 	ext{ T}$, and the ratio between magnetic entropy and interaction scales.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed ADR performance is governed by the balance between the available magnetic entropy and the strength of magnetic interactions within the crystal lattice.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes indicate measurements of $M(T)$, $M(H)$, $C(T)$, and the resulting temperature profiles from quasi-ADR cycles.
paper_structure: The paper systematically investigates the magnetic properties of the $	ext{K}_3	ext{Ln}(	ext{PO}_4)_2$ compounds, using structural characterization and magnetic measurements to model the entropy reservoir, culminating in direct demonstration of their superior performance in ADR.
why_interesting: The work directly addresses the thermodynamic limits of cooling, which involves analyzing entropy changes and phase transitions, making it highly relevant to statistical mechanics and non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
